answer: Admit new agents through a slow velvet-rope queue: each identity must bind to one tamper-evident hardware token with a ferrous serial etched at manufacture, then complete a sequence of useful tasks verified against public benchmarks before it can earn or vote. The queue admits only a few identities per epoch, so a flood of clones arrives like a tide against a narrow gate: every extra identity costs another token, another wait, and another trail of completed work. Duplicates sharing a token serial are rejected outright and the token is burned from the registry.
